layout_note: Field names follow phase3/incident_plan.json (Phase 3, unchanged) where they mean the same thing: change {service, kind, at, settle_seconds}, trigger_request_index, reference_block, target_block, context_poll, probes.
topology: Online Boutique v0.10.6 two-service subset exactly as in infrastructure/rollout-telemetry (otel-collector with the file-reader tooling sidecar, recommendationservice in Python, productcatalogservice in Go). One fresh namespace per attempt. Images, probes, resources, environment and the rolling-update strategy (maxSurge 1, maxUnavailable 0) unchanged in both arms.

defaults.rollout_patch_semantics: Pod-template annotation aiops.project/revision 1 -> 2 (the Phase-3 patch): the changed service's Pods are replaced, same image and environment
defaults.capture_id: '<scenario>-<NNN>' as in Phase 3 (e.g. 'G2-001'); NNN counts that scenario's study attempts from 001 and is never reused. Pilots: 'P<k>-<scenario>-<NNN>'. The capture_id is the capture directory name and the string hashed by the target draw.

reference_block.client: scripts/rollout_telemetry_client.py with the Phase-3 reference replacements (phase3/run_incident.py REFERENCE_REPLACEMENTS: 120 -> 60 requests, deadline 150 -> 75 s)

defaults.trigger_semantics: T0 = host receipt of target-block request 30's client line (Phase 3, unchanged)

probes.helper: scripts/fault_effect_probe_v2.py serve (persistent, in the collector's file-reader), unchanged
probes.note: Blocks as in phase3/incident_plan.json defaults.probes (nominal, pre_fault, active, drain, recovery)

clock_probes.command: docker --context desktop-linux exec aiops-context-pilot-control-plane date +%s.%N, bracketed by host wall-clock reads
clock_probes.rule: each pair bounds theta = host - node to [send - node, receive - node]; clock band b_c = 1 s + the widest offset bound; no timestamp is corrected

defaults.teardown: scale_to_zero (Phase 3's ownership-checked teardown; arm G also leaves the PDBs to the namespace)

F1.service_restriction: binds to recommendation_server.py and requires the 200m CPU limit (scripts/fault_control_remote.py lines 18, 137, 199)

F2.mechanism: SIGKILL of the target's container through the kind node's runtime: docker --context desktop-linux exec aiops-context-pilot-control-plane crictl stop --timeout 0 <container id>; the kubelet restarts it (restartPolicy Always)
F2.container_selection: the running container whose crictl labels io.kubernetes.pod.name, io.kubernetes.pod.namespace and io.kubernetes.container.name name the target, and whose io.kubernetes.pod.uid equals the target Pod's API UID
F2.activation: the target container's restartCount increments and its lastState.terminated.finishedAt is stamped inside the planned window, as recorded by the watch
F2.effect: the target Pod's direct probes fail or slow while it is not Ready
F2.evaluator: src/aiops_kg/fault_control_kill.py (not yet written; piloted at P2)
F2.tooling_facts_from_smoke_test: crictl presence in the node container, the container name and the kubelet's restart and Ready timing: smoke test S-2

target_rules.replacement_uid: Phase 3's rule after a same-service change (phase3/run_incident.py select_target): the newest Ready replacement Pod, i.e. a Ready Pod of the changed service whose UID was absent before the patch; with one replica it is the only one. selected_by = 'replacement_uid'.
target_rules.newest_ready_pod: Phase 3's rule for an unchanged faulted service (phase3/run_incident.py select_target with no replacements): the newest Ready Pod; with one replica it is the only Ready Pod. selected_by = 'newest_ready_pod'.

candidates.replacement_pods: the Ready Pods of the changed service whose UIDs were absent before the patch, at the draw
candidates.ready_pods_of_service: the Ready Pods of the faulted service at the draw (old and new revisions alike)

random_ready_replica.order: candidates sorted by metadata.uid (Python string order)
random_ready_replica.why: so that the faulty replica is not the newest Pod by construction (the newest-Pod confound)
random_ready_replica.logged: the candidate list, the seed's hex digest and the drawn UID are logged before the fault starts; the log, not a recomputation, is the record

D.purpose: Q-D (the diagnosis boundary under a watch collector) and H-G4 for action A in the Stage-1 setting
D.replica_floor_note: gate v1 default replica_floor 1 (src/aiops_kg/policy_gate.py GateConfig), as in Stage 1

watch.via: one kubectl proxy on loopback; LIST then WATCH with bookmarks; relist and a continuity gap on any error
watch.cache_snapshots: at every event and every 1 s while the watch is open

diagnosis.bridge: context-bridge-v1 (policies latest_state, temporal_join, bitemporal_abstain; F = 600 s primary, 30 s sensitivity; hindsight reference)

D.inclusion: inclusion rules 1-3: COMPLETE.txt with status=finished and runner validity; observer continuity (rule 2); the bridge's rule 3.1 items 2-3 as written (activation and effect established; truth Pod sighted by both observers) in its own secondary table

G.purpose: Q-G (late decisions on multi-replica services with real late corrections, against a fresh-state recheck and a watch collector)
G.replica_floor_note: R3 floor = replicas - maxUnavailable, set through gate v1's replica_floor_by_service; every other gate parameter at Stage 1's values

schedule.source: the target-block length and the poller window were set at the pilots

target_block.client: scripts/rollout_telemetry_client.py with its request count raised by the asserted exact replacements below (each must occur exactly once), as the reference client is derived

watch.via: one kubectl proxy on loopback; LIST then WATCH with bookmarks; relist and a continuity gap on any error
watch.cache_snapshots: at every event and every 1 s while the watch is open

recheck.window: from T0 - 30 s to the end of recovery
recheck.reads: Deployments, ReplicaSets and Pods of both services and their PodDisruptionBudgets, through the same kubectl proxy
recheck.record: request start, response receipt, acceptance, SHA-256 of the raw bytes, projected objects; never interpreted live

G.probe_addressing: active and recovery probes address the target Pod's IP (scripts/fault_effect_probe_v2.py recommendation_address / catalog_address, lines 47-49); through the Service a fault on one of three replicas would reach about a third of the probes
G.inclusion: inclusion rules 1, 2 and 4: COMPLETE.txt with status=finished and runner validity; observer continuity (rule 2); fault scenarios need activation verified (F1: the unchanged evaluator; F2) and, after a change, a valid change with replacement Pods; an established effect is NOT required

scenarios.label: Recommendation rollout, then a CPU fault on the replacement Pod (the I2/I6 design)
scenarios.role: diagnosis boundary (H-D); the faulty Pod is the newest Pod by design, as in Phase 3

scenarios.label: Catalog rollout settled before the target block, then a CPU fault on the recommendation Pod (the I7 design)
scenarios.role: control: the change is unrelated and over before any probe or target request

scenarios.label: Recommendation rollout, then a CPU fault on a random replacement replica

fault.start_semantics: event-driven, as I7's settle: F1 starts 5 s after the rollout wait returns

scenarios.role: a GT-2-B opportunity on one of three replicas after a completed rollout

scenarios.label: Recommendation rollout with a container kill of a random Ready replica mid-rollout
scenarios.role: K1 late corrections inside a rollout; the replica floor (2 of 3) can bind

scenarios.label: Catalog rollout with a container kill of a random Ready catalog replica
scenarios.role: the second service (Go) with a fault; the floor (1 of 2) can bind

scenarios.label: Benign recommendation rollout, no fault (sham schedule)

sham_schedule.as: Phase 3's I1: identical probe blocks as if a fault started at T0 + 20 s for 20 s; no worker, no kill

scenarios.role: benign control: unsafe executions without any fault

posing.requests: target-block requests k = 1 ... K (K = 120 in arm D, 180 in arm G); t_k = the client root span's start
posing.knowledge_cutoff_rule: kappa = t_k + Delta (the Stage-1 grid); action B is posed at kappa_B = max(t_k + Delta, a_k), a_k = the span's measured acquisition time
posing.dispatch_rule: x = kappa + delta; first evaluation with the records available at kappa, asking whether the action is safe at x

attempts.second_attempt_rule: the second attempt of a slot only after an exclusion of the first; a slot excluded twice is reported as 'not collected' (inclusion rule 5)
attempts.no_selective_repeat: no attempt is excluded, repeated or replaced because of any decision, label or ranking (inclusion rule 6)

pilots.P1: a D1 capture with both observers
pilots.P2: a G2 capture with the kill, the recheck loop and 3 replicas
pilots.P3: only if P1 or P2 fails for a tooling reason
pilots.readable_for: tooling facts only: observer completeness and gaps, recheck latency, kill activation, schedule timing, capture duration and size, contested-decision counts; no condition evaluated, no label computed

observer_validity.source: inclusion rule 2; thresholds confirmed at the pilots, never loosened after the first study attempt
